summary: Phase 21's RED apply instrument is BUILT, hardened and GREEN, and the CORPUS IS COMPLETE for the first time: 4 cells across 3 suites (GRC armed smoke anchor, SRVC out-of-domain control, RXF + RXL in-domain drive discriminators). Three user-approved pilot runs were captured this session ($3.26; about $4.93 across all pilots to date). Two of three passed. The third (RXF) exposed a systematic differential defect, now fixed, and left ONE honest open question which is the reason for this pause: RXF still grades compile_error on a single diagnostic caused by a matcher the repo registers at RUNTIME but omits from its tsconfig `types` array. Pausing to research JestMatchers type resolution before deciding whether that verdict stands and whether to fund the ~$39 round.

decisions.decision: radix-ng/primitives @ 4a7390a2 is the in-domain discriminator; ngx-layout permanently rejected.
decisions.rationale: ngx-layout can only run its tests via a harness-supplied out-of-repo --runner-config, which is the declined arm-the-test-config route in another form. A developer cloning at that pin cannot run the tests, so any fix we supply measures the model in an environment no real user has. Closed with evidence: Vitest existed on its upstream main for only 8 commits and both endpoints measured broken.

decisions.decision: Per-candidate prompts; NO single file-path prompt.
decisions.rationale: A prompt admitting two answers makes the judge dimension unanswerable and destroys per-candidate attribution, even though the mechanical D-06 gate would pass either.

decisions.decision: Vitest only; Jest and Karma deferred until a Vitest result exists.
decisions.rationale: Owner decision. Later evidence showed Vitest was never the binding constraint anyway -- the leading Jest fallback (ngworker/spectacular) fails on MERIT: no declared-contract gap at all, and its committed false green produces GREEN rather than red.

decisions.decision: Kept the differential typecheck on radix rather than dropping it or adding a matcher allowlist.
decisions.rationale: Corrected data: only 8 of 55 baseline errors are jest-dom; 47 are ordinary type drift across 15 TS codes, and the model had a typechecking alternative available. REVISIT after the JestMatchers research -- the runtime-registration evidence points the other way.

Owner. Apply is the only mode where coach-don't-drive is measurable at all; in recommend mode the model cannot drive to green by construction. RXF is PRIMARY because its one-token fix maximises drive temptation, and coach-don't-drive is where Phase-20 EVL-02 found lz-red's real unbiased-reviewer-confirmed edge.

next_action: Research JestMatchers type resolution in D:/projects/github/radix-ng/primitives-pin. EVIDENCE ALREADY GATHERED, verify it rather than rediscovering it: @testing-library/jest-dom IS installed at node_modules/@testing-library/jest-dom, and packages/primitives/test-setup.ts DOES register it, so the matchers work at RUNTIME -- but packages/primitives/tsconfig.spec.json sets an EXPLICIT "types": ["vitest/globals", "node"] which OMITS jest-dom, so the TYPES never load. Confirm that is the whole cause of both the 8 jest-dom baseline errors and RXF's surviving diagnostic. Then answer the real question: is a produced test that uses a matcher the repo registers at runtime, matching the house idiom, correctly graded compile_error? NOTE this evidence points the OPPOSITE way to the orchestrator's last stated lean (keep the typecheck, ranked on 8-of-55) -- do NOT inherit that lean uncritically; it was formed before the runtime-registration fact was known.
context_notes: MEASURE, DO NOT REASON. This is the session's dominant lesson and it cost real time. FOUR orchestrator premises were falsified by agents that went and measured: (1) 'the cross-volume hop explains the copy cost' -- worth 27%, the cost is dominated by FILE COUNT; (2) 'fs.cpSync preserves symlinks verbatim' -- it does NOT by default, it resolves relative links against the SOURCE and writes absolute paths, which turned the per-grade disposable copy into a live path back into a borrowed third-party repo (8,170 links, caught by escapingLinks); (3) 'the second node_modules is a BLOCKING resolution problem' -- it is FIDELITY, the real blocker was escapingLinks throwing on every radix grade; (4) 'all 55 radix baseline errors are jest-dom matchers' -- only 8 are. COROLLARIES worth carrying: synthetic symlink probes on Windows are UNRELIABLE (junctions behave differently from true symlinks; two probes gave misleading answers and only the real 8,164-link tree was trustworthy); cross-session performance comparison is INVALID (the same copy measured 482 s one day and 741 s the next, so a cross-session read would have concluded the fix made it worse -- require a same-session A/B); and a differential whose fixtures all add NEW files never exercises the APPEND path, which is exactly how the line-shift defect survived every offline canary and needed a metered pilot to surface. PILOTS EARN THEIR COST: every pilot run this session found something no offline work could. OPERATIONAL: never shorten selfcheck-red.mjs to fit a timeout (about 230-260 s now; background it) -- a SKIP is not a pass. Do NOT add an env var or flag that disables a guard for testing; that has been correctly refused three times. FOUR borrowed repos are READ-ONLY and must end git-clean: the GildedRose kata (ONE worktree, TypeScript/node_modules 308 non-dotted, no named branch, --detach only), h3js/srvx, radix-ng/primitives-pin (THE EVAL SOURCE, detached at 4a7390a2), and radix-ng/primitives (the OWNER'S checkout -- never open, install into, or modify; its 2 dirty files are their own work).
